evidenceClaims.statement: A persistent unexplained adult lateral neck mass needs malignancy evaluation even when infection improves or imaging shows fluid.
evidenceClaims.limitation: No universal duration cutoff or cancer probability.

evidenceClaims.statement: Contrast-enhanced neck CT can characterize a nonthyroid, nonparotid mass and deep cervical extent when superficial imaging is incomplete.
evidenceClaims.limitation: A suitable offered study, not universally superior to MRI or mandatory before needle sampling.

evidenceClaims.statement: FNA is an appropriate initial cell acquisition for an undiagnosed adult cervical mass; open biopsy is a later resort.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single adequate guideline. Selected core can also be appropriate and is not offered as an incorrect alternative. Not a lymphoma-excision rule.

evidenceClaims.statement: Cyst-fluid cytology may fail to represent a cervical lesion; ultrasound guidance can direct needle sampling to tissue.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Cross-checks retained F05. No universal core-over-FNA superiority after one fluid pass.

evidenceClaims.statement: Suspected peripheral T-cell lymphoma generally needs surgical biopsy for architectural, immunophenotypic and molecular assessment when surgery is possible.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single current specialty guideline. Not every lymphoid node; limited needle samples do not establish subtype.

evidenceClaims.statement: Transoral extraction can preserve the gland for symptomatic fixed distal submandibular duct stones when basket retrieval is unsuccessful.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Depends on access and operator expertise; no universal size threshold or mandated procedure ladder.

evidenceClaims.statement: An asymptomatic intraparenchymal salivary stone may be managed conservatively; a residual image finding does not itself require gland removal.
evidenceClaims.limitation: No fixed follow-up interval or guarantee against recurrence.

evidenceClaims.statement: Core sampling can provide histological information when salivary-gland FNA does not establish diagnosis or histotype.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Not superior to every optimized FNA. Does not justify an unsafe route. Open biopsy of an intact major gland is generally avoided.

evidenceClaims.statement: Contrast MRI is preferred for cross-sectional local assessment of suspected major salivary malignancy.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Neck/skull-base coverage is an original clinical application to nerve symptoms; CT complements bone assessment and PET serves systemic staging.

evidenceClaims.statement: A functioning facial nerve separable from a parotid malignancy can be preserved during complete tumor resection.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Do not sacrifice based on proximity alone. Functioning nerves with gross invasion are a separate withheld boundary.

evidenceClaims.statement: Microscopic perineural growth supports postoperative local radiotherapy discussion after salivary cancer resection.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Predominantly retrospective evidence. No dose, treatment-start interval or survival benefit invented.

evidenceClaims.statement: Routine addition of chemotherapy to postoperative salivary-gland radiotherapy has no established benefit in the ESMO guideline.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single guideline; does not prohibit a clinical trial or individualized oncology decision.

evidenceClaims.statement: CT or ultrasound can assess suspected parotid abscess; limited surface imaging does not settle an unexplained deep infection.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Current ESR/ESHNR guidance supports contrast CT for deep infection and distinguishes it from superficial ultrasound. Contrast MRI can also be appropriate; duct-only or unenhanced studies have different scope.

evidenceClaims.statement: Deep cervical infection can extend into the mediastinum; new thoracic findings require assessment beyond the visible neck.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Not every chest symptom indicates mediastinitis; airway and circulation assessed separately.

evidenceClaims.statement: Infected deep neck or mediastinal collections require drainage planning with relevant surgical teams alongside antimicrobials.
evidenceClaims.limitation: No ranking of open versus thoracoscopic approach or universal anatomic cutoff.

evidenceClaims.statement: Stridor or dyspnea with deep neck infection warrants urgent airway assessment rather than routine outpatient imaging.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Unscored safety boundary; no precise airway technique prescribed.

evidenceClaims.statement: Gustatory sweating can occur as a complication after parotid surgery.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Agenda only; no scored medication ranking from this general summary.

evidenceClaims.statement: CT assessment of complicated deep neck soft-tissue infection uses intravenous contrast to assess enhancement and complications.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Contrast MRI is also a suitable deep-infection modality. No universal CT superiority or fixed acquisition time.

evidenceClaims.statement: Suspected descending mediastinal extension requires chest coverage in addition to the cervical source region.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Source imaging extent follows the suspected involved compartments, not a blanket chest CT for uncomplicated infection.

evidenceClaims.statement: Facial weakness or sensory symptoms accompanying a salivary mass raise concern for malignant involvement.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Symptoms are not histological proof or an automatic indication for nerve sacrifice.

evidenceClaims.statement: The mediastinum occupies the central thoracic region between the lungs, distinct from the lungs themselves.
evidenceClaims.limitation: This basic compartment definition does not determine a specific operative access route.

evidenceClaims.statement: Dedicated local head-and-neck imaging addresses anatomical extent, whereas systemic staging investigates disease beyond the primary region.
evidenceClaims.limitation: The appropriate studies depend on malignancy, stage and clinical question; no universal PET or CT sequence.

evidenceClaims.statement: An accessible distal submandibular duct stone is suited to a duct extraction approach rather than extracorporeal fragmentation.
evidenceClaims.limitation: A site/access distinction, not an efficacy percentage or universal size-based algorithm.

evidenceClaims.statement: Gland removal is reserved for selected persistent symptomatic stone disease after suitable gland-preserving options.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Depends on symptoms, anatomy and available expertise; does not prohibit resection for another indication.

evidenceClaims.statement: Superficial ultrasound cannot reliably exclude extension of neck infection into deeper spaces beyond its acoustic window.
evidenceClaims.limitation: This is a coverage limitation, not a claim that every ultrasound is nondiagnostic.

evidenceClaims.statement: Before duplicating a CT examination, check what prior imaging was acquired and whether it can answer the current question.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single government guidance source for avoiding duplicates. Retrieval in R01 is conditional on documented completed contrast acquisition, relevant coverage, unchanged clinical state and access to that study; never a reason to delay urgent assessment.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in specialist head-and-neck assessment; exact synthetic case observations require clinician review.

evidenceClaims.statement: A sample from a different cervical node does not establish the diagnosis of the unsampled index neck mass.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Target-specific inference from image-guided neck-mass sampling principles, not a quoted diagnostic-accuracy estimate. A benign result must be tied to the actual sampled lesion; no universal FNA-versus-core hierarchy.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in specialist head-and-neck assessment; exact synthetic case observations require clinician review.

evidenceClaims.statement: New focal cranial-nerve dysfunction with a salivary malignancy warrants assessment for neural spread; focused contrast MRI should examine the relevant nerve course beyond the gland when that course was not included previously.
evidenceClaims.limitation: UK guideline supports malignant neurological warning findings and MRI; independent open review supports course coverage. Clinical weakness suggests but does not prove spread. CT can complement bone evaluation, and a prior complete adequate MRI may be reviewed instead of repeated.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in specialist head-and-neck assessment; exact synthetic case observations require clinician review.

evidenceClaims.statement: A facial nerve divided during parotid surgery should be considered for immediate repair; direct repair requires approximation without tension, with an interposition graft considered when direct tension-free repair is not possible.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single current multidisciplinary guideline for this exact repair distinction. No numerical gap cutoff, guaranteed recovery, or permission to sacrifice an uninvolved nerve is implied. Exact viability and repair plan require specialist assessment.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in specialist head-and-neck assessment; exact synthetic case observations require clinician review.

evidenceClaims.statement: Availability of a viable proximal facial-nerve stump and identifiable distal branches supports facial-to-facial grafting; donor-nerve reanimation may be considered when a suitable proximal facial stump is unavailable.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single current multidisciplinary guideline. Technique selection is individualized; the synthetic iatrogenic division is separate from the disputed functioning-but-grossly-invaded nerve boundary.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in specialist head-and-neck assessment; exact synthetic case observations require clinician review.

evidenceClaims.statement: CT assessment of complicated neck soft-tissue infection uses intravenous contrast timed for soft-tissue venous-phase evaluation; suspected descending spread requires coverage through the chest.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single current specialty practice recommendation for phase selection; independent NHS guidance supports deep-neck complications and CT assessment but does not adjudicate every acquisition phase. An arterial vascular question would require a different tailored protocol.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in specialist head-and-neck assessment; exact synthetic case observations require clinician review.

evidenceClaims.statement: Weakness of muscles producing facial expression can indicate dysfunction of the facial nerve motor pathway.
evidenceClaims.limitation: One independently licensed specialist review directly links facial-expression weakness to CN VII. The constructed upper/lower facial examination does not establish a malignant cause by itself.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in specialist head-and-neck assessment; exact synthetic case observations require clinician review.

evidenceClaims.statement: Loss of facial sensation in the distribution of a trigeminal division can indicate dysfunction of that division.
evidenceClaims.limitation: One independently licensed specialist review directly describes the sensory distributions. Symmetric light touch does not exclude every possible trigeminal abnormality, and the competing pathway is not treated as impossible.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in specialist head-and-neck assessment; exact synthetic case observations require clinician review.

withheldDisagreements.statement: Gross invasion of a still-functioning facial nerve during parotid cancer surgery.
withheldDisagreements.boundary: UK favors resection of confirmed invaded or encased branches. ESMO describes individual decisions with normal function and macroscopic invasion. No automatic preservation-versus-sacrifice key for this setting.
withheldDisagreements.ownerQuestion: Melissa: for a future exact case with normal function and confirmed gross invasion, which branch-resection versus preservation decision, histology and goals should be taught?
